sentences.text: Levnesovia is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur classified within the superfamily Hadrosauroidea and the clade Hadrosauromorpha.
The type species of the genus, which is the specimen-based species name for the group, is L. transoxiana, honoring Russian paleontologist Lev Nessov and the ancient region of Transoxiana.
This animal holds the distinction of being the oldest well-documented taxon referable to Hadrosauroidea.
Adults are distinguished from younger relatives by a high sagittal crest on the parietals and the absence of dorsal vertebrae spines ending in tubercles.

Fossils found in the Bissekty Formation of Uzbekistan include partial skulls, jaws, and numerous postcranial bones from an animal that lived between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago during the Turonian stage.

It is debated whether Levnesovia, Bactrosaurus, and Gilmoreosaurus represent the earliest radiation of Hadrosauroidea, which may have occurred during the Cenomanian-Turonian in Asia and possibly North America.
